hamster-slots.blurb: A cute pixel-art idle slot machine, powered by a hamster on a wheel. Spin the reels, win (pretend) coins, buy upgrades and teach your hamster to run the wheel by itself. Then retire to the Big Cage, grow the Family Tree and eventually open a whole hamster casino.
highlights: Eight slot machines, a jackpot wheel and a card gamble
Every sprite and sound is made in code, no game engine
hamster-slots.imageAlt: Hamster Slots: a BIG WIN on the Snack Stacker, with coins flying everywhere

does.title: Spin the reels
does.text: Eight slot machines, from Old Clunky to the Hamster Maze, with wilds, free spins, a jackpot wheel and a card gamble. All the coins are pretend.

does.title: Upgrade everything
does.text: Payouts, auto-spin, Luck and new symbols for the hamster and every machine. The Hamster Helper buys the cheap ones for you.

does.title: Retire and start again
does.text: Retire to the Big Cage, plant Heirloom Seeds in the Family Tree and, one day, move the whole family to a new colony for perks that last forever.

does.title: Open a casino
does.text: Roulette, blackjack and a hamster derby for pretend chips, then your own Family Casino that earns Takings while you're away.

does.title: Never get lost
does.text: A little guide tells you what to try next, and every new thing gets a brass padlock that springs open.

how.title: You spin
how.text: Each spin picks the reels from a seeded random roll and pays by the machine's rules: paylines, ways or hold & spin.

how.title: The rules decide
how.text: All the game's maths lives in `src/logic/` and never touches the page, so the tests and the balance simulator run it without a browser.

how.title: The view draws it
how.text: Sprites are drawn as text in `src/view/art.ts`. The bigger scenes are painted pixel by pixel in code and every sound is made in the browser. No game engine.

how.title: It saves itself
how.text: Progress is kept in your browser and keeps earning a little while you're away. Menu, then Save backup, gives you a code to move it elsewhere.

pip.blurb: A tiny pixel-art jellybean who lives on your desktop. Pip trots about on four stubby legs, climbs the edges of your screen, naps when you wander off and keeps a gentle eye on your breaks, your Pomodoros and whether you've had any water lately. He's a desktop pet, not a productivity nag. (That's him walking around up the top, too.)
highlights: Nine flavours, from cherry to candy cane
Never steals focus or blocks your screen
pip.imageAlt: Pip, a cherry-red pixel jellybean with four stubby legs

does.title: Lives on your desktop
does.text: Pip trots along the bottom of your screen, climbs the edges, naps when you wander off and greets you when you're back.

does.title: Reacts to you
does.text: Hover and hearts pop, click for a remark, double-click for a snack, drag him about. Click him five times fast and he huffs off.

does.title: Looks after you
does.text: A gentle Pomodoro timer, break reminders and a nudge to drink water, with a four-week calendar of how you did. Never a nag.

does.title: Dresses for the season
does.text: Nine flavours, from cherry to candy cane, and he wears bubblegum in February, pumpkin in October and candy cane in December.

how.title: The main process decides
how.text: Everything in `src/main/` is plain code with no Electron in it: the clock and the randomness are passed in, so Pip's brain is easy to test.

how.title: The renderer draws
how.text: One transparent, always-on-top window covers your work area. It ignores the mouse everywhere except Pip himself, found by checking the alpha of his current sprite frame.

how.title: A bridge in between
how.text: `preload.js` is the only way across, with an explicit list of allowed channels. Every timer comes from a stored start time, so closing your laptop mid-Pomodoro can't corrupt it.

how.title: He notices you
how.text: Activity is read from the system's idle time every ten seconds. Five quiet minutes and he curls up to sleep; any movement wakes him within a second.

highlights: A dark Live board that fills in ticker by ticker
Missing numbers stay blank, never made up
stock-review.imageAlt: A sketch of the Stock Review live board: a list of watchlists on the left, a table filling in ticker by ticker, and Run and Copy for AI buttons

does.title: Ranks a whole market
does.text: Point it at a watchlist, an index or about a thousand names across the world and it scores every stock from 0 to 100.

does.title: No AI, no guessing
does.text: Scoring is plain Python: the same data in always gives the same ranks out. Missing numbers stay blank, they are never made up.

does.title: Writes one tidy file
does.text: The whole ranked universe lands in a single compact Markdown file, built to hand to an AI of your choice for a second opinion.

does.title: Checks itself
does.text: Every run is stored by date and a backtest asks whether higher scores ever really came before higher returns.

how.title: Collect
how.text: It pulls prices and fundamentals for your list from yfinance, caching per ticker per day and retrying politely when Yahoo pushes back.
how.note: just run it again to fill gaps

how.title: Rank
how.text: Each metric becomes a 0 to 100 percentile against the rest of the universe. Fundamentals are ranked within their sector, so banks are not judged against software.

how.title: Score
how.text: Category scores (fundamentals, technicals, momentum, analyst) are weighted into one number. If a stock is missing something, its weight is shared out over what it does have.

how.title: Report and backtest
how.text: Everything goes into one Markdown file and a date-stamped database, and `run_backtest.py` tests whether the score predicted anything.
